task_id: R-01 / conditional unused-chip CS pull-up feasibility
status: User stopped for day; breadboard/resistors/grabber ordered, not received; preferred U2-target/U1-grabber test remains unassembled/unverified
owner_inventory: Owner confirms no resistors; asks whether Pi can supply variable resistance. Existing Dupont leads and spare full-size clips; breadboard/secure connection not confirmed.

Pi_substitute.decision: No suitable GPIO/software-only substitute for a passive pull-up to the flash rail.
Pi_substitute.reason: RP1 pad settings enable pull-up/down and drive strength; they do not supply a configurable two-terminal resistor to an external 1.8 V rail. Pi 5 GPIO runs at 3.3 V; direct weak pull-up may overvoltage the flash if loading changes. Changing RP1 threshold registers does not change its physical supply.

conditional_topology.active_programmer_clip: NEXT intended setup: short clip on U2 via checked1.8Vadapter. CURRENT end state: both clips removed/everything disconnected/Pi off.
conditional_topology.auxiliary_access: If both clips fit without stress, use spare full SOIC-16 clip on U1 with independently checked physical pin-to-terminal mapping. Only two leads used; other contacts externally disconnected/insulated.
conditional_topology.connection: U1 physical pin 2/VCC -> resistor -> U1 physical pin 7/CS. This uses the existing target 1.8 V rail, not Pi 3.3 V/5 V.
conditional_topology.pin_number_warning: Physical 16-pin Micron package numbers, not adapter OUTPUT numbers or assumed ribbon order.
conditional_topology.purpose: Bias unused U1 CS high while U2 is selected; this is not physical isolation and may fail against board loading.

candidate_first_diagnostic.component: Fixed through-hole10kOhm1%1/2W resistor from owner-ordered assortment, small solderless breadboard and actual ordered ICgrabber; inspect/measured before use.
candidate_first_diagnostic.basis: Conservative bounded added-current starting experiment, not inferred from unpowered 4.35/4.8 kOhm equivalents or claimed vendor-approved Cisco repair. Unknown board paths mean efficacy/safety cannot be guaranteed solely from resistor current.
candidate_first_diagnostic.not_selected: No lower-resistance escalation, variable-potentiometer wiper, direct CS-to-VCC jumper, Pi pull-up or added power source.

staged_checks: Wait for owner to resume and parts to arrive. No additional hardware task, power-up, background SSH or tests today.

Reconfirm chassis FDO2742M0FK, board, physical target U2, current normal-power/cable/CR2032/CH341A isolation, Pi supply and exclusive programmer/console ownership. Current end state is all disconnected, not a live U2 harness.

With every source unplugged/residual0V, inspect actual grabber model/tip/termination and breadboard; meter the chosen fixed 10k resistor and record lead baseline. Verify breadboard five-hole groups/rail breaks rather than assuming layout.

Dry-fit programming clip on U2 and insulated single-leg grabber on unused U1pin7; confirm orientation, eight existing flash-signal routes and no bridge/leg stress. Pin7 is dot-side upper-row second from left in IMG_1289. Do not force fit or hold a loose connection by hand during acquisition.

If secure fit exists, assemble mapped P1pin1/flash1.8V -> fixed10k resistor on breadboard -> grabber -> U1physicalpin7/CS. Programming harness remains Pi->1.8Vadapter->U2. Pi3.3V/5V are not this pull-up source. Leave other pins unchanged; do not tie CS directly to VCC.

Verify unpowered resistor/connection paths and no unintended short before reconnecting only the checked official-PSU/Pi/adapter setup. Check loaded P1 rail 1.7–2.0V and U1 idle CS with no SPI. A 10k pull-up is an experimental limited load, not assured isolation/repair.

If baseline acceptable, prepare one bounded no-clock U2-CS control with cleanup/report retrieval that can be verified despite SSH loss. Meter U1CS during idle/asserted/released states and P1 supply; verify selected U2 CS at a safe accessible mapped endpoint when possible. Restore/check driver/node and exclusive ownership. No automatic read follows.

If U1CS still falls or connection/power is unstable, stop this bias approach; do not automatically decrease resistance, increase voltage, add speculative selector/reset jumpers or power the router normally with the programmer attached.

Only after independent selection is adequately supported, run explicitly requested U2-labelled bounded RDID/read-only samples at multiple addresses/transfer shapes and independently compare originals. Stable DC alone does not prove waveform quality or read accuracy.

If bounded acquisition is repeatable and plausible, plan separate pairs of full33554432-byte reads per physical chip, privately preserving originals/hashes/logs and unique board/security data before any write decision. U1/U2 contents need not match each other.

U1 acquisition is a separate unresolved access problem: do not assume the reverse grabber-onU2/clip-onU1 arrangement fits or is proven by U2 success. If inaccessible, evaluate a verified larger CS contact or suitable rework assistance for a temporary lead/isolation/off-board reading; do not improvise leg lifting/trace cutting.
limits: No resistor exists in current inventory, so no wiring/test can proceed yet.
A pull-up test measures response to a known limited load; it cannot identify a specific active driver or prove complete electrical isolation.
DMM spot measurements do not certify fast transitions/clocked signal margins.
If secure bias/control cannot be established, separately read chips off-board using suitable rework assistance; do not recommend inexperienced leg lifting/trace cutting.
